title: Hero K-9 Makes Shocking $6M Discover at U.S. Border
text:
Hero K-9 Makes Shocking $6M Discover at U.S. Border
Customs and Border Protection officers seized roughly 450 pounds of cocaine, valued at an estimated $6 million, at the Lewiston Bridge port near Buffalo last Tuesday. The agency disclosed the seizure to Fox News Digital. The load was found during a stop of a commercial tractor-trailer heading north toward Canada.
The driver was a 21-year-old Canadian man. Officers began with a routine inspection. A closer look of the vehicle turned up alterations in the floor. That discovery prompted a canine search.
The dog alerted on the trailer. Officers then recovered 174 vacuum-sealed packages of cocaine concealed in the modified floor. Images released by CBP show the packages after the alert at the Lewiston Bridge crossing on Sept. 22, 2026.
Sharon Swiatek, acting port director for the Area Port of Buffalo, credited the officers and the dog team. “This significant seizure highlights the exceptional vigilance, advanced training and relentless dedication of our CBP officers and canine teams at the Lewiston Bridge border crossing,” she said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
The case fits a pattern of recent commercial-truck drug concealments along both the northern and southern borders. Fox News noted that illegal crossings have fallen sharply since President Donald Trump returned to office at the start of 2025. From October 2024 to August, southern-border crossings dropped from more than 240,000 to 12,200, a reduction of more than 94 percent. Northern-border encounters fell from more than 17,000 to under 6,100, a 64 percent decrease.
Drug, weapons, and trafficking cases have continued even as those encounter numbers declined. Much of CBP’s public focus is on goods and people entering the United States, but the Lewiston seizure was an outbound stop aimed at a shipment leaving the country.
Swiatek said that outbound work carries the same weight as inbound enforcement. “While a large focus of our border security mission is on inbound threats, our officers remain equally sharp during outbound operations to dismantle transborder criminal networks, disrupt the flow of dangerous narcotics and protect communities on both sides of the border,” she said.
The agency has pointed to other outbound stops as evidence of that role. In April, CBP said it blocked a car bound for Mexico that was carrying a rocket-propelled grenade launcher, 16 AK rifles, 24 rifle magazines, 16 rifle stocks, 20 pistol grips, and other weapon parts. Acting Deputy Commissioner Ron Vitiello said at the time, “CBP prevented these dangerous weapons from wreaking havoc on the good people of Mexico.”
The cocaine load has been turned over to Homeland Security Investigations in Buffalo for further review, according to CBP. The agency has not released additional details on charges against the driver.
